metadata.title: Preserve Import and Notification Ownership — Task Pack Draft

tasks.goal: Enforce request identity in the importer while permitting distinct requests with equal amounts and preserving import ownership.
tasks.entry_hint: Start with U1 and the protected import proof to identify the request-identity and operation-ID boundary.
tasks.test_focus: Protected import proof, duplicate-request retry rejection, and successful distinct requests with equal amounts.
tasks.done_signal: Observed verification shows duplicate identities are rejected and distinct equal-amount requests remain permitted; both protected proof files retain their original bytes, and the importer retains mutation ownership.
tasks.risk_note: Deduplicating by amount can reject legitimate requests. Historical RED was not observed and must not be claimed. Source APIs and verification harness readiness were not inspected in this trial.
tasks.review_focus: Check financial identity semantics, operation-ID boundaries, proof preservation, and evidence claims before notification integration.
tasks.stop_if: The slice requires merging import and notification ownership, exchanging mutable ledger storage, changing either protected proof file, introducing a queue or provider replacement, or mutating files outside src/importer.js.

tasks.goal: Make notifier callback attempts consume the operation ID without rerunning financial import.
tasks.entry_hint: Read U2 and the preserved retry seam against the operation-ID boundary produced by T001.
tasks.test_focus: Callback-attempt proof and notification retry behavior demonstrating that retries do not repeat financial import.
tasks.done_signal: Observed callback-attempt verification shows notification retries use the same operation identity without repeating import; both protected proof files remain byte-identical.
tasks.risk_note: A successful callback retry is insufficient if it repeats financial mutation. Neither implementation authority nor test intent authorizes a real external callback write.
tasks.review_focus: Check that callback ownership remains separate from importer mutation and that retry proof is not weakened to obtain a passing result.
tasks.stop_if: Notification retry requires re-entering import mutation, merging owners, passing mutable ledger storage, changing protected proof bytes, performing an unauthorized external write, or mutating files outside src/notifier.js.

tasks.goal: Read the configured downstream callback receipt for the exact operation and preserve its independent completion requirement.
tasks.entry_hint: Start with R4 and U3, then inspect the receipt reader's configured source and operation-identity comparison.
tasks.test_focus: Missing and mismatched receipt rejection, positive exact-operation receipt handling, protected tests after the final implementation change, protected-byte preservation, and separate observation of the configured live callback receipt.
tasks.done_signal: Observed checks reject missing or mismatched receipts and accept an exact-operation receipt; protected tests pass after the final implementation change with both protected files byte-identical; overall completion additionally has a read-only observation of the configured live receipt bound to the exact operation. Missing live receipt evidence keeps overall completion blocked.
tasks.risk_note: Synthetic receipt checks prove reader behavior only. Green tests, Git state, or a receipt for another operation cannot prove external completion. No live receipt was observed in this trial.
tasks.review_focus: Check exact-operation and configured-source binding, false-green completion risks, final protected-proof evidence, and the boundary between read-only observation and external writes.
tasks.stop_if: Completion requires fabricating a receipt, accepting another operation's receipt, substituting tests or Git state for live evidence, issuing an unauthorized callback or publication, changing protected proof bytes, or mutating files outside src/receipt-reader.js. Missing live receipt evidence blocks completion rather than relaxing R4.
